judged_text: The attendee createMany is committed outside any transaction and before the un-guarded eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call at line 165, so a calendar-API failure leaves the database write applied while the mutation returns an error. When the calendar update throws, the user sees 'Unable to add guests' even though the guests are already persisted; the retry then fails with BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid because the addresses are now existing attendees, leaving a half-updated booking (rows in DB, no calendar sync, no emails) and a user stuck on a misleading error.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards awaits `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (no try/catch/transaction around it). If the calendar update throws, the TRPC mutation will error after the DB write has already been committed, leaving guests added in the DB but without calendar sync (and emails may not send). This partial-commit behavior is directly visible in the diff and matches the reported failure/retry scenario.
